title: fix(telegram): sending to topic 0 delivers, then fails with a topic mismatch
body:
Closes #146442

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram send or typing action aimed at topic 0 (`-100123:topic:0`, `-100123:0`, or a `threadId` of 0) is sent to Telegram as if it were a real topic. Topic ids start at 1 (General). Per the review of #146442, Telegram treats 0 like "no topic", so the message can land in General and OpenClaw then reports a topic mismatch after delivery.

## User Impact

Topic 0 is now rejected before anything is sent or looked up. Lower-level send and typing errors name the topic ID; the CLI resolver retains its generic invalid-target error. Valid targets, including General topic 1, behave as before. I found no internal path that produces topic 0 (topic ids from inbound updates come from Telegram and start at 1), so the only behavior change is for callers that pass 0 themselves: they get an immediate error instead of a delivery followed by a mismatch error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forum topic ids are positive integers, as channel Direct Messages topic ids already were. The target parser now requires a positive id for every topic form. Explicit thread options (`threadId` from tools, `messageThreadId`) go through the same check for sends and for typing, and that check now runs before the chat lookup, so a bad option cannot cause a `getChat` request or a target write-back. When the topic is what was rejected, the error says so instead of blaming the chat id. General still sends `message_thread_id: 1` for typing, which the docs call out and a test now pins.

## Evidence

- **Real send boundary:** `send.history.test.ts` drives `sendMessageTelegram` and `sendTypingTelegram` through grammY against the local Bot API stand-in (`useTelegramHttpFixture`, a real HTTP server). For seven zero-topic inputs it asserts the topic error and zero requests: forum marker, shorthand, internal group form, username target, numeric thread option, a thread option before a username lookup, and a thread option beside a valid topic target.
- **Fails before the change:** I ran the original six cases against the unmodified production files with the tests kept. All six fail: the send goes out and OpenClaw reports `Telegram delivered message 902 to topic unknown; expected topic 0 | CHANNEL_PARTIAL_DELIVERY` (the stand-in answers like the Bot API server does for `message_thread_id=0`, per the source trace in the #146442 review). The seventh case and the topic-specific message were added after review and each failed before its fix (typing let an explicit 0 through next to a valid topic target; target-form zero reported "numeric chat ID").
- **Parser:** the existing topic-id table in `targets.test.ts` now covers the forum zero forms and fails on the old parser (`-1001234567890:topic:0` parsed as topic 0). A small truth table covers `hasRejectedTelegramTopic`, including garbage base targets that must keep the plain invalid-recipient error.
- **Cost (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <files> --maxWorkers=1`):** the seven new send-boundary cases take 10-13 ms each (about 80 ms in total) inside `send.history.test.ts`. That file's existing SQLite and HTTP cases (about 2 s each) are unchanged and already put it over 30 s, so this PR adds roughly 80 ms to a file that was already the slow owner. `targets.test.ts` runs 22 tests in about 26 s wall including first-run transform. Nothing uses real timers, sleeps or polling.
- **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` passes on the final diff: extension and extension-test typechecks, lint, dead-export scan, ratchets, format, and the import-cycle and boundary guards. `autoreview` (P2) is scoped-clean on the final diff. Its earlier rounds found three real issues (typing ignored an invalid explicit option next to a valid topic target, a misleading generic error, and a classifier that blamed the topic for garbage targets), each fixed test-first and covered above. It also claimed typing could still send for a rejected topic target; the executed tests show it throws before any request.
- **Sibling tests with this change:** all pass.
  <details>
  <summary>Details</summary>

  - `send.telegram-http`, `send.recovery.telegram-http`, `reply-scaffolding.telegram-http`: 130 tests
  - `send.proxy`, `transport-payload`, `outbound-adapter.sanitize`, `send.transport-close-proof`, `action-runtime`: 62 tests
  - root tests through the real plugin (`telegram-history-read`, `outbound-sanitize-text-delivery`, `loopback-ask-user-telegram-channel`): 15 tests
  - `send.history`: 34 tests; `targets`: 22 tests
  - Windows only: the four `bot-message-context.*` inbound-admission files fail at fixture setup with `EPERM, Permission denied` on their own temp directory. One of them fails identically (8 of 8) on unmodified `main` code, so this is not caused by the change, and CI on Linux does not hit it.
  </details>

## Maintainer live Telegram proof (2026-10-02)

Compared built main `4b2fccac77a3c9f7efc793e62ac3222cca66be41` with exact PR head `8ae92e67b1f9e47e8c5701176bb1454d6309d323` in an isolated Docker container, using the repository Telegram Test Server userbot runner, Convex-leased credentials, separate profiles (`p146442base` / `p146442cand`), and TDLib recording. No model calls were made.

The leased chat is a basic group (`type=group`, `isForum=false`). It was not converted or otherwise changed.

Command on both refs (target redacted):

```sh
openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> message send --channel telegram \
  --target '<group>:topic:0' --message '<unique-zero-marker>' --json
```

| Observation | Main | PR head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI zero-topic exit | 1, **after delivery** | 1, **before delivery** |
| CLI error | `OutboundDeliveryError: Telegram delivered message 6331 to topic unknown; expected topic 0` with `CHANNEL_PARTIAL_DELIVERY` | `Unknown target "<group>:topic:0" for Telegram. Hint: <chatId>` |
| TDLib zero-marker message | Observed at +2346 ms, no topic | Absent throughout the completed 90-second recording |
| Plain group send control | Exit 0; TDLib observed at +4163 ms | Exit 0; TDLib observed at +3839 ms |
| Proxied `sendMessage` requests | 2: zero-marker plus plain control | 1: plain control only |

The CLI resolver uses its existing generic invalid-target error. The lower-level `sendMessageTelegram` / `sendTypingTelegram` paths expose `Telegram topic ID must be a positive safe integer.`; the HTTP-boundary regression covers that distinction. We did not change the resolver or claim its error is topic-specific.

**Regression:** the candidate's `send.history.test.ts` copied onto pinned main produced exactly seven zero-topic failures (all reported delivery followed by the expected-topic-0 mismatch), with 27 other cases passing. On the candidate, all 34 send-history cases and all 22 target cases passed. Candidate combined wall time: 35.82 s; baseline file: 34.51 s. An initial candidate setup run overlapped its build and was invalidated by the compiler input-snapshot guard; the recorded passing run started after the build finished.

**NOT-RUN:** forum General delivery, `:topic:1`, and a real non-zero forum-topic control. No forum credential was available from the leased tester group. The live trace proves the zero-target misdelivery and prevention on a basic group, not forum routing compatibility; General remains covered by the existing HTTP-boundary control.

Both runner scopes removed their credential/Gateway scratch and released their leases. All three proof messages were deleted through TDLib using their recorded account-scoped receipts. No persistent group settings were changed.

No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes in the touched-file history check.

Thanks to @adamczhang for the fix and @aniruddhaadak80 for the report.
